machine: generic CI-class x86_64 / local arm64 — gzip default level (-6); CI enforces on ubuntu-latest

toolchain.note: the crate sets wasm-opt = false so wasm-pack does not auto-fetch binaryen; the size-optimized .wasm is produced by running wasm-opt -Oz separately (see reproduce below)

budget.ceiling_note: measured optimized-gzipped (~843 KB) + ~15% headroom; CI fails the wasm job if the optimized gzipped .wasm exceeds this ceiling

gating_decision.rationale: Per-language gating is not the size lever. The 8 per-language pattern files are 0.7-16 KB each; the embedded person-name corpora gzip-floor at ~140 KB; the remaining bulk is language-independent compiled code (fancy-regex backtracking engine, unicode-normalization tables, sha2/sha3/hmac, serde/ron). wasm-opt -Oz strips ~129 KB of raw code but leaves the gzipped size essentially flat, confirming the weight is the shared code+data floor, not language data. Embedding all 8 languages keeps the in-browser API at parity with the Python fast mode for a one-time, HTTP-cached load. Future size reduction is a code-level effort (regex engine, dependency trimming), not language gating.

reproduce: cargo install wasm-pack --locked   # or jetli/wasm-pack-action in CI
wasm_opt_features_note: wasm-opt is invoked with the modern wasm feature set explicitly enabled (bulk-memory, nontrapping-float-to-int, sign-ext, mutable-globals, reference-types, multivalue) because recent LLVM emits these by default; without them wasm-opt 130 fails input validation on memory.copy / bulk-memory ops.
